historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name Rafaaq as a sub-district within the Maghreb region during his travels in the 14th century. It was part of the Emirate of Tlemcen and is described as a fertile region with numerous gardens and crops.

Al-Bakri mentions Rafaaq as a town and port located on the Atlantic coast of present-day Morocco, important for its agricultural produce and trading connections with the Iberian Peninsula in the 11th century.
